issuer: Driver and Vehicle Licensing, States of Guernsey (Edward T Wheadon House, St Peter Port)
note: The States of Guernsey's Driver and Vehicle Licensing pages and documents (read 2026-10-30). Its category and age entitlements document gives category B (car) from 17; a full licence is applied for after passing the driving test on a provisional licence, from one month before the minimum age. The fees page charges 'First Provisional, Renewal or Exchange' at £20.40 for a licence issued for 3 years or less and £6.80 a year (or part) for longer, but names no fee for the first full licence issued after the test, so the fee is null rather than that line read across. Full licences are 'normally issued for a maximum of 10 years to expire the month prior to a decade birthday', shortened by age, categories or medical conditions: the term varies with the holder's age, which the form can't hold, so it is null. The exchange list (last updated 07/2025) is held: those whose licences may be exchanged in all categories (the EU and EEA states listed, Gibraltar, Great Britain and Northern Ireland, the Isle of Man, Jersey), those for motorcycle or car categories (Andorra, Queensland, Western Australia, Barbados, the British Virgin Islands, the Cayman Islands, the Falkland Islands, Hong Kong, Japan, Monaco, Singapore, South Africa, the UAE, Zimbabwe), car categories (the Faroe Islands, Korea, Moldova), and automatic categories only unless a manual test is shown (the other Australian states and territories, Canada as its provinces and territories, New Zealand, North Macedonia, Ukraine, Taiwan); a translation or certificate some of them need isn't held. Switzerland ('certain categories ... advice will be given') is left out. Guernsey issues no identity card here. The form's fee by the year and term to an age (2026-10-30) don't hold Guernsey's either: the £6.80 a year is the provisional's, renewal's and exchange's line, not the first full licence's (the apply page says only 'We will contact you for payment if this is required'), and the term ends the month before a decade birthday, not at one fixed age.
